title: Show every tool call on its own row instead of folding runs of them into one summary
description:
The main screen folds runs of tool calls — reads, searches, directory listings, the read-only shell commands behind them, MCP calls, memory, workshop and scratchpad writes, task and todo tools, REPL, and in fullscreen other shell commands — into one summary line. With this patch none of them fold: each shows as an ordinary tool row with its result. Thinking between them still folds into its own 'Thought for Xs' line, and PreToolUse hook summaries and recalled memories are handled exactly as upstream handles them.

The fold is a grouping pass over the message list, and it carries more than tool calls. Thinking blocks are absorbed into the same groups, and a group's summary line is the only place the main screen shows thinking — a raw thinking block renders nothing outside Ctrl+O or verbose mode. An earlier version of this patch dismantled groups wholesale, which made every thought invisible and dropped hook summaries absorbed mid-group. This one leaves the grouping pass untouched and only stops tool calls from being admitted to it: each call becomes a break point, and everything else groups as before.

sites.description:
The function the grouping pass asks whether a tool call may join a fold. It is the only point in the chain used for nothing but grouping: the classifier behind it is exported and also feeds the renderer and the recent-activity display, so changing the classifier would reach those too. This one is called only by the grouping pass's per-message cache, and returning null here is how it already says 'not foldable' for any tool it does not recognise.

Identified as the two-parameter function that handles grouped_tool_use and returns the fold record — toolUseIds, readPaths, isAbsorbedSilently among its fields.

verify.describe: tool calls are no longer admitted to a fold
